messages:
Sam: quick check — split-bench with mixed int4 + fp8 fallback shows a 6-8% quality regression on some long-tail prompts. anyone seen similar noise?
Sam: command used: ```./bench --model llama-2-chat-13b --quant int4 --fallback fp8 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --prompts-file ./inputs/longtail.json```
Tanya: is that vs fp8-native or int8 baseline? do we have exact ppl numbers? :eyes:
Sam: compared to fp8-native baseline. sample median ppl: fp8-native 12.6, int4+fp8-fallback 13.4. distribution skew on ~3% of samples.
Kevin: can you paste the failing prompt ids? might be prompt-length or instruction style skew.
Sam: pasted a few ids in the run artifact: https://perf.redwood/runs/1968abc (see failing_ids.txt). short example: "legal Q&A with repeated citations and long context buffers"
Oliver: did you run KV cache warm vs cold? cold cache sometimes changes quant behavior for long histories.
Sam: ran both; delta persists more on warm cache at tail tokens. strange.
perf-bot: note — run used runtime kernel v2.3.1 on g5-48x, quant-plugin v1.5. Logged artifacts at https://perf.redwood/artifacts/1968abc/
Maya: can we get a token-level profiling trace (kernel switch events + quantization-error heatmap)? @Kevin @Tanya
Kevin: I can capture timeline + per-token log. scheduling profiler now; will dump within 2 hours.
Tanya: also suggest creating an "edgecase" prompt cluster to verify whether fallback heuristic is mis-triggering. Sam, can you open a small PR with the prompt matrix?
Sam: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/2446 — added matrix and test harness, marked as WIP.
Oliver: pinging infra — can we reserve dedicated instances for deterministic re-runs (no noisy colocated tenants)? Need g5-12x + g5-24x for 2-hour window tonight.
infra-bot: reservation confirmed for 20:00 PT — instances: g5-12x (id g5-12-a) and g5-24x (id g5-24-b).
Kevin: plan — reproduce, collect flame + kv events, check kernel v2.3.0 (older) vs v2.3.1. if it's kernel-induced, roll back to v2.3.0 for canary.
Tanya: temporary mitigation: gate fp8 fallback behind perplexity delta > 0.5 so we don't flip kernels for small deltas. if that buys time, we can avoid product regressions.
Sam: ownership: Kevin + Tanya to triage; Sam to curate promptset and collate artifacts. I'll post a short summary in #quant-results after the run. :thumbsup:
Kevin: if it's fallback noise we should also consider a deterministic fallback threshold tied to sequence position (only allow fallback after token 128).
Tanya: agreed. will prototype thresholds in the PR.
Sam: thanks all — will update here once the profiler dumps land.
